title: UX Writing
summary: UX writing helps users understand tasks, decisions and recovery through concise, consistent language.

MUST.text: Name the user's task or outcome in the user's vocabulary; avoid internal system names.
Use one canonical term per concept across labels, messages, docs and support.

SHOULD.text: Lead with the action or outcome; put qualifying detail after.
Use sentence case and active voice; keep sentences under ~20 words.

AVOID.text: Avoid promotional filler, cleverness, jargon and unexplained abbreviations.
Avoid ambiguous pronouns and generic link text such as "click here" or "learn more".

DECIDE.decision: Choose one canonical term and reuse it
Define on first use in user language
Match the user's state, not brand voice

FAILURE_MODES: Jargon passes review but blocks task completion.
Inconsistent terms make search and help fail.
Clever copy hides the action behind wordplay.
Overlong copy breaks scanning and localization.
